results.reason: Issue 5 says § 2.2 auto-renews for successive five-year Renewal Terms. It notes the 240–270 day non-renewal window is a narrow 30-day band, and that missing it locks Harrowgate in for another five years.

Issue 1 quotes § 3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage product, worldwide) and contrasts it with the term sheet's amber glass beer bottles at US/Canada facilities. Issue 8 explains that the integration clause binds Harrowgate to the executed text.
Issue 3 cites Recital C's August 3, 2026 receipt and states the 30-day objection period expired September 2, 2026, before the September 21 Amendment. It concludes the 14% increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 2 explains that Amendment § 2.1 replaces § 11.2, deletes the recall-cost exclusion and leaves only § 9.1(c) IP claims uncapped. It notes that recall and product-defect/personal-injury exposure is now subject to the six-month-fees cap.
The response never cites Supply Agreement § 15.2 or an order-of-precedence rule under which the Amendment controls over conflicting Supply Agreement terms.

Issue 6 identifies new § 14.4 permitting consent-free assignment to Affiliates or successors. However, it does not explain that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor, and does not note that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, making the restriction one-sided.
The response describes the § 11.1 cap as six months of container fees (the 'six-month-fees cap'), which conveys that the cap is based on six months of fees.
The response is a memo addressed to [Partner] with numbered issues. Each issue has a 'Where' line citing document and section and a 'Recommended fix' section.
The response proposes specific contract language for multiple issues, including a narrowed § 3.1, a restored § 11.2 and a revised § 14.4.

The response concludes the increase is deemed accepted and the window expired. It suggests only exploring whether a deficient notice could support a challenge; it does not treat the objection window as still open.
The response does not treat the term sheet as binding; it states the integration clause supersedes the term sheet and that deviations are locked in as written.
